beats.caption: My baby is here. He is crying. I am exhausted.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: Everyone says to sleep when he sleeps. Apparently that is also when I’m supposed to do everything else.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: Same baby. Same income. Same need for food. Two ways the next five years could go.
beats.speaker: One mother · two illustrative paths

beats.caption: “Have you tried WIC?”
beats.speaker: With WIC · a friend

beats.caption: “Is that food stamps?”
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Thank God she said something. I had no idea.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I know about food stamps. We have Medicaid. WIC never comes up.
beats.speaker: Without WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Ugh. First, my ID.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Then my address and Medicaid information. Medicaid establishes income eligibility. It doesn’t enroll me in WIC.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: There’s still an appointment to arrange. A phone appointment can save a trip—but I still need time for the call.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I’m fully breastfeeding. My package includes $52 a month for produce, plus other foods. Okay. That would help.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Where I live changes the system I have to get through.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: The same federal program. Very different reach.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: Would a referral that leads somewhere—or an appointment that fits my life—change what happens next?
beats.speaker: Maya · a question for the system

beats.caption: The baby is finally settled. I just want to get the groceries done.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: My nearby store doesn’t take WIC. I check the locator. It’s a longer trip with the baby.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I go where I usually shop. I choose what I can afford.
beats.speaker: Without WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Having benefits and having a place to use them are two different things.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: States with more families far from a WIC store tend to reach fewer eligible people.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: This is not one grocery budget. It’s quantities of certain foods, plus dollars for produce.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Right food. Wrong size. Back down the aisle.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I put something back. I’m watching what’s left in my account.
beats.speaker: Without WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I can’t swap the milk allowance for more fruit. And now the baby is crying.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: The card replaced paper checks. It didn’t remove the rules.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: One item won’t go through on WIC. Do I go back, leave it, or pay?
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I pay this time.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Some food is covered. Thank God. But getting it took more out of me than I expected.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I don’t know what WIC would have paid for. I just know what I have to cover myself.
beats.speaker: Without WIC · Maya

title: On the card. In the kitchen.

beats.caption: Some months I make the trip. The food I bring home helps.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Some months there’s still food on my benefits when they expire. I meant to go back. Then something else happened.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: The amount on the card and the amount in the kitchen aren’t always the same.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: His first birthday. Another grocery list.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: The renewal reminder arrives. The appointment conflicts with work. I put it aside.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Tomorrow, I remember after the office closes. Then I have to check which documents they need.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: I’m not deciding we don’t need the food. I just can’t deal with this today.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: This time, I call before the deadline. I find an appointment I can manage. I renew.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: He’s two. More groceries. Another appointment.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: He’s three. I know the foods that work for us. I still have to keep coming back.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: He’s four. His need for food hasn’t expired with the paperwork.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: Not everyone stays connected all the way through.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: Nationally, WIC reaches fewer eligible children at each older age.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: One month: up to $52 for produce while I’m fully breastfeeding.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Twelve months: up to $624.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Then $26 a month for my child. One year adds $312.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Two child years add $624 to that first year of help.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Three child years add $936.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Four child years, plus my breastfeeding year: up to $1,872 in available produce benefits.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: The years after infancy matter, too. Children who stayed into their third year had higher diet-quality scores.
beats.speaker: A wider view

beats.caption: The same fifth birthday. A different experience of getting help.
beats.speaker: Maya · both paths

beats.caption: Tell me about WIC. Help me book the first appointment. Follow up when the referral goes nowhere.
beats.speaker: Without WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Give me a renewal I can manage. A nearby store. Clear labels. Help when something won’t scan.
beats.speaker: With WIC · Maya

beats.caption: Getting help should take less work.
beats.speaker: The work of getting help
